audit_status.source_base: Hebrew Exodus / Shemot text tradition, Song of the Sea poetic layer; draft aligned to public-domain comparison layer later
audit_status.review_note: First-pass draft reviewed for Song of the Sea, Miriam, women with timbrels, Marah, healing statute/testing.

familiar.text: Then sang Moses and the children of Israel this song unto the LORD, and spake, saying, I will sing unto the LORD, for he hath triumphed gloriously: the horse and his rider hath he thrown into the sea.

familiar.text: The LORD is my strength and song, and he is become my salvation: he is my God, and I will prepare him an habitation; my father’s God, and I will exalt him.

verses.restored: YHWH is man of war; YHWH is his name.

familiar.text: The LORD is a man of war: the LORD is his name.

familiar.text: Pharaoh’s chariots and his host hath he cast into the sea: his chosen captains also are drowned in the Red sea.

familiar.text: And in the greatness of thine excellency thou hast overthrown them that rose up against thee: thou sentest forth thy wrath, which consumed them as stubble.

familiar.text: And with the blast of thy nostrils the waters were gathered together, the floods stood upright as an heap, and the depths were congealed in the heart of the sea.

familiar.text: Thou didst blow with thy wind, the sea covered them: they sank as lead in the mighty waters.

verses.restored: You stretched out your right hand; earth swallowed them.

familiar.text: Thou stretchedst out thy right hand, the earth swallowed them.

verses.restored: In your loyal love you led the people whom you redeemed; in your strength you guided them to your holy habitation.

familiar.text: Thou in thy mercy hast led forth the people which thou hast redeemed: thou hast guided them in thy strength unto thy holy habitation.

familiar.text: The people shall hear, and be afraid: sorrow shall take hold on the inhabitants of Palestina.

familiar.text: Then the dukes of Edom shall be amazed; the mighty men of Moab, trembling shall take hold upon them; all the inhabitants of Canaan shall melt away.

verses.restored: Terror and dread fell upon them; by greatness of your arm they became still as stone, until your people passed over, YHWH, until people you acquired passed over.

familiar.text: Fear and dread shall fall upon them; by the greatness of thine arm they shall be as still as a stone; till thy people pass over, O LORD, till the people pass over, which thou hast purchased.

familiar.text: And Miriam the prophetess, the sister of Aaron, took a timbrel in her hand; and all the women went out after her with timbrels and with dances.

familiar.text: And Miriam answered them, Sing ye to the LORD, for he hath triumphed gloriously; the horse and his rider hath he thrown into the sea.

familiar.text: So Moses brought Israel from the Red sea, and they went out into the wilderness of Shur; and they went three days in the wilderness, and found no water.

verses.restored: They came to Marah, but they could not drink waters of Marah, for they were bitter; therefore its name was called Marah.

familiar.text: And when they came to Marah, they could not drink of the waters of Marah, for they were bitter: therefore the name of it was called Marah.

verses.restored: The people grumbled against Moses, saying, What shall we drink?

familiar.text: And the people murmured against Moses, saying, What shall we drink?

verses.restored: He cried to YHWH, and YHWH showed him a tree/wood; he threw it into waters, and waters became sweet. There he set for him statute and judgment, and there he tested him.

familiar.text: And he cried unto the LORD; and the LORD shewed him a tree, which when he had cast into the waters, the waters were made sweet: there he made for them a statute and an ordinance, and there he proved them,

verses.restored: He said, If listening, you listen to voice of YHWH your Divine, and do what is straight in his eyes, give ear to his commands and keep all his statutes, then all the diseases I placed upon Egypt I will not place upon you, for I am YHWH your healer.

familiar.text: And said, If thou wilt diligently hearken to the voice of the LORD thy God, and wilt do that which is right in his sight, and wilt give ear to his commandments, and keep all his statutes, I will put none of these diseases upon thee, which I have brought upon the Egyptians: for I am the LORD that healeth thee.

verses.restored: They came to Elim, and there were twelve springs of water and seventy palms; and they camped there by waters.

familiar.text: And they came to Elim, where were twelve wells of water, and threescore and ten palm trees: and they encamped there by the waters.

translation_notes: Song of the Sea is ancient victory poetry; preserve its intensity while not turning it into ethnic hatred.
Ruach/wind/breath imagery links sea deliverance to Divine power.
Miriam is explicitly prophetess and leads women with timbrels and dances; preserve her leadership.
Marah moves from victory song to wilderness thirst; YHWH as healer closes the chapter.
The tree/wood sweetening bitter waters should be preserved without over-allegorizing in the source layer.
safety_note: The victory song celebrates liberation from Pharaoh's chariot army, not hatred of Egyptians as a people. Violent poetic imagery should be read as ancient liberation hymn against oppressive military pursuit.
